clue.text: Notice split is wide of the mark

parts.note: an advertisement or notice, shortened to ad
a split or breach is a rift

explanation.surface: Someone sees a crack in a sign and declares it a miss.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wide of the mark has drifted off target, so it is astray in that idiomatic sense.

clue.text: Breaking up is great

definitions.meaning: splitting apart, as ice or a voice does

explanation.surface: A cheerful verdict that a split is a fine thing.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is fracturing with a sharp sound; the other is British slang for excellent.

clue.text: Hen bit some sparrow in garden

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A hen pecks at a sparrow in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A limb of a chicken served as food is a part, or bit, of the hen.

clue.text: Old war horse's place to claim local prize

indicators.note: to claim means to take in and hold, so the first word wraps around the second

parts.note: the wooden horse of the Trojan War stood at Troy
a local is a pub, abbreviated PH (public house)

explanation.surface: A retired warhorse's home is said to claim a pub prize.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'local' is a Briton's neighbourhood pub; PH is the map abbreviation for public house.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup or similar award is a prize given to a winner.

clue.text: Fruit far from a peach, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is chosen for how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a peach is a beauty, so far from one is unattractive or plain

explanation.surface: Someone compares a fruit unfavourably with a peach.
explanation.definitionFit: The ugli is a Jamaican citrus hybrid, a tangelo, so it is a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Preferred US city, seeing Brazilian shantytown

parts.note: a preferred thing is a favourite, informally a fave
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: Someone's favourite American city is linked to a Brazilian slum.
explanation.definitionFit: The Portuguese word for an informal hillside settlement in Brazilian cities.

clue.text: Selling of clothes, classic in fashion

indicators.note: in places the classic word inside the fashion word

parts.note: the rage is the current fashion
traditional, shortened to trad

explanation.surface: A classic look is in vogue in the clothing business.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal name for the garment industry, the business of making and selling clothing.

clue.text: Riders e'er reckless as those upon the saddle?

definitions.note: plural: the parts of riders that sit on the saddle

indicators.note: reckless suggests wild, careless disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Riders who were ever reckless, sitting in the saddle.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: not the riders themselves but the bottoms resting on the saddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Backsides are the body parts a rider sits on, the bits literally upon the saddle.

clue.text: Drugs at an increased level, put your foot down

parts.note: speed is slang for amphetamine drugs
raised or higher means up

explanation.surface: A driver, high on drugs, is told to accelerate.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting your foot down on the accelerator pedal means going faster.

clue.text: Horse caught by a horse back in the country

indicators.note: caught by means held inside the following letters
back means the pair is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a nag is an old horse
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: One horse is captured by another in some country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns A NAG into GANA; H goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A West African nation on the Gulf of Guinea.

clue.text: Characters at the back in Saudi Arabian music video twerking under assumed names

indicators.note: characters at the back are the final letters of each word that follows

explanation.surface: A Saudi music video features twerking by performers using false names.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for incognito: travelling or acting while concealing one's identity.

clue.text: Commander in chief available to embrace Independence Day, for starters

indicators.note: to embrace means to hug, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: someone available is present

indicators.note: for starters takes the opening letter of each of those words

explanation.surface: The commander in chief is free to celebrate Independence Day.
explanation.definitionFit: The US head of state is constitutionally the supreme commander of the armed forces.

clue.text: Figure drinking first of sherries, dry

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the letter goes inside the number

parts.note: a number, here thirty

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of the word sherries

explanation.surface: Someone downs sherry, and a dry one at that.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry means wanting a drink, parched.

clue.text: L'Escargot caught up by Italian stallion

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top
caught by the words means the letters are held within Italian stallion

explanation.surface: A racehorse named L'Escargot is beaten by an Italian stallion.
explanation.walkthrough: L'Escargot was a famous racehorse, fitting the horse theme, but here it is just French for the creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Escargot is the French word for the edible garden mollusc.

clue.text: Little scene, as Christian priest drops cap

parts.note: Christian Dior, the French fashion designer

indicators.note: drops cap means the head, the opening letter, is removed

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist priest

explanation.surface: A Christian priest loses his hat in a small tableau.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Christian' suggests religion beside 'priest', but it is the designer's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A miniature three-dimensional model of a setting is a small scene.

clue.text: Cat in Australia, briefly?

definitions.meaning: the snow leopard is also known by this name
Australia is known as Oz, and oz is the short form of this unit of weight

explanation.surface: Asking whether a cat lives in Australia, in a nutshell.
explanation.definitionFit: The snow leopard has this alternative name; the weight unit abbreviates to oz, Australia's nickname.

clue.text: Rider, evidently weary? Difficult to grip a horse

indicators.note: to grip means to hold inside, so the first word goes around

parts.note: difficult means hard
gee-gee, a child's word for a horse, gives GG

explanation.surface: A tired jockey struggles to stay in control of a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: H. Rider Haggard was the author of King Solomon's Mines; the definition plays on his surname also meaning worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: The novelist named Rider bore a surname meaning gaunt and exhausted-looking.

clue.text: Player ideally taken off — or a match abandoned?

indicators.note: abandoned means let loose or wild, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A player is substituted, or else the match is called off.
explanation.definitionFit: An overacting performer is a player the audience would like removed from the stage.

clue.text: Frank, perhaps, in frightful joint, loosely speaking?

indicators.note: loosely speaking says the words only roughly sound like the answer when said

parts.note: frightful is dire and a joint is a wrist

explanation.surface: Someone called Frank sits in an awful pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' hints at a dodgy bar, but it is a body joint; Anne Frank kept a famous diary.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne Frank is the best-known example of someone who kept a journal.

clue.text: Style required long past eternal youth

indicators.note: past means beyond, so this piece comes after the other

parts.note: Peter Pan is the boy who never grew up
to long for something is to ache for it

explanation.surface: A style is needed that long outlasts youth.
explanation.definitionFit: Flamboyant confidence of manner, flair.

clue.text: Horses caught Shergar far from stable

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: far from stable means unsteady and disordered, so the letters shift

explanation.surface: Racehorses are found while the stolen Shergar is missing from the stable.
explanation.walkthrough: Shergar was a Derby winner famously kidnapped in Ireland in 1983.
explanation.definitionFit: Chargers are warhorses, horses ridden into battle.

clue.text: Punk on grey with a bit of a brain

parts.note: Punk is the setter, so the setter refers to himself as me
grey and dull both describe a cheerless sky

explanation.surface: A punk with grey hair has a bit of a brain.
explanation.definitionFit: The medulla oblongata is a part of the brainstem.

clue.text: Everyone breaking down upset, in US city

indicators.note: breaking means splitting the other word open
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: feeling down is feeling sad
everyone means all

explanation.surface: Everyone is breaking down, upset, in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns SAD into DAS; ALL breaks it open.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Texan metropolis is one American city among many.

clue.text: Horse able to manoeuvre during swim, doing the backstroke?

indicators.note: during means within the time of, so the letters go inside
going backwards means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a quick swim is a dip

indicators.note: to manoeuvre means to move around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A horse is able to swim backstroke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doing the backstroke?' reverses the swim word, so PID; 'to manoeuvre' scrambles ABLE to IEBAL, which goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A piebald is a horse with patches of black and white.

clue.text: Chicken — don't push it through one's ears!

indicators.note: heard through the ears means the sound, not the spelling, counts

parts.note: the opposite of push is pull, so this is pull it

explanation.surface: A warning not to push a chicken through one's ears.
explanation.definitionFit: A pullet is a young hen less than a year old.

clue.text: European houses chuffed at first with Russian principal in Nijinsky, perhaps?

indicators.note: with means accompanied by, so this piece is added on
houses means holds within

parts.note: a Dane is a European from Denmark

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of chuffed

parts.note: R is a standard abbreviation for Russian

explanation.surface: A European is delighted with a Russian racehorse.
explanation.walkthrough: Nijinsky was both a racehorse and the ballet star; the second is meant. Chuffed is British for pleased.
explanation.definitionFit: Vaslav Nijinsky was a celebrated principal of the Ballets Russes, an example of a ballet performer.

clue.text: Divine end to piece captured by a cellist in rhapsody

indicators.note: captured by means held inside the other letters
in rhapsody suggests wild free-flowing music, so the letters are rearranged
end to takes the last letter of piece

explanation.surface: A cellist ends a piece in a rapturous, heavenly performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavenly, belonging to the sky or heaven, hence godlike.

clue.text: Chasers out, yet to beat Never Say Die

indicators.note: to beat means to batter, so the letters are knocked about and rearranged

explanation.surface: Steeplechasers are out, yet a horse named Never Say Die beat them.
explanation.walkthrough: Never Say Die was a Derby winner, but here the phrase is the definition: refuse to give up.
explanation.definitionFit: Never giving in is persisting to the end, an idiom from horse racing.

clue.text: Continue to shake as a carriage

parts.note: a dog wags or shakes its tail
to continue is to go on, so on alone

explanation.surface: Something keeps rocking like a horse-drawn vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A four-wheeled vehicle for goods, drawn by horses, is a kind of carriage.

clue.text: Wild horse overly accelerating initially — stop!

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: A rider shouts at a runaway horse picking up too much speed.
explanation.definitionFit: The call used to make a horse halt.

clue.text: Old US state, not in the style of 12

indicators.note: not means without, so those letters are removed

parts.note: Alabama is a southern US state
the French phrase a la means in the style of

explanation.surface: A former US state that is unlike some leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 refers to the answer at 12 across, a head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: Barack Obama was the 44th US head of state.

clue.text: See 26
